name: AllTogether: Investigating the Efficacy of Spliced Prompt for Web Navigation using Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AllTogether standardizes prompts for HTML-based web navigation and compares prompting with instruction fine-tuning. Its analysis examines how HTML context, interaction history, and current environmental feedback affect task execution.

name: Training a Vision Language Model as Smartphone Assistant
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains a smartphone assistant from sequences of screenshots paired with earlier actions. The model predicts UI-only interactions such as taps and swipes, with evaluation on Android in the Wild.

name: Identifying User Goals from UI Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Defines goal identification from observed UI trajectories and an evaluation method for comparing intent descriptions within the same interface context. Experiments reuse Android and web automation data to compare human and model inference of users’ detailed goals.

name: Dynamic Planning for LLM-based Graphical User Interface Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Dynamic Planning of Thoughts revises a mobile GUI plan using current environmental feedback and execution history. The study compares this planning strategy with long-dialogue prompting and examines its behavior on unfamiliar tasks and different language-model backbones.

name: Lightweight Neural App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LiMAC combines a compact Action Transformer with a fine-tuned vision-language model for Android app control. It uses textual goals and histories of screenshots and UI trees to predict actions, with evaluation on two mobile-control datasets.

name: From Context to Action: Analysis of the Impact of State Representation and Context on the Generalization of Multi-Turn Web Navigation Agents

summary: Analyzes how interaction history and webpage representation affect multiturn web-agent generalization across unfamiliar websites, task categories, and geographic settings.

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.

name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.

name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.

name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.

name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.
